pillarForecast.why: Blast immunity is his own hero exception; expect it to be absorbed with at most one clause of approval, and no complaint that it's unfair in his favour.
Chains in every run keep his favourite payoff; near misses reward the out-turn itself, which he already perceives as the clever act.

Slow-mo changes the game's clock under his thumbs. Fired once it reads as a highlight; fired repeatedly as a pack streams past from behind it can read as stutter or lag and pull attention to the timing.
With blasts in every run and none hurting him, crowds clear more easily; a deep run may draw 'a bit easy' early (he said so in run 50), though chasers still kill him most runs.
Same v11 B pressure from behind; near misses put even more focus on them roaring past.
Difficulty matches v11 (bots 3.4-3.7); expect at least one sector-6 run or a win, likely via the sector 4 checkpoint.

biggestRisk: The near-miss slow-mo stuttering the flow. Pursuers come from behind and stream past him, so in a crowd several grazes can fire back-to-back: time keeps dropping to 30% in the middle of the risky quick turn he likes. If that reads as lag rather than as a cinematic beat, the thing meant to answer 'one more thing' becomes an interruption of his favourite movement (P7), and he'll ask to shorten or remove it.
abVerdict: Mild preference for B, and about half the time he names it: slow-mo and CLOSE! are loud and visible, but they're our idea, not his, so expect less certainty than v11's blasts. Most likely: praise on the first B run ('the slow motion when one roared past was cool'), then a qualifier on a later B run (stuttery in packs, or a tweak to its length). ~20% he notices its absence on an A run; ~30% he never mentions it and results are a tie.
